category.bottomContent:
What You Need to Know About Accounting Software

What is Accounting Software?

Accounting software is software that automates accounting and bookkeeping tasks like invoicing, accounts payable, accounts receivable, income, and expenses. Small business accounting software puts all your financial information in one place, making it easier to share data across teams or externally and saving your employees from double entries or having to type things in manually.

The best accounting software for small business comes in 2 forms: desktop accounting software or online accounting software. Desktop accounting software is an application you install on your company’s computers. Online accounting software, also known as software-as-a-service or SaaS, has the same functions but runs on the cloud.

What Features Should You Look for in Your Accounting Software?

At a minimum, your accounting software is an online bookkeeping program that carries out the core accounting processes we mentioned earlier–such as invoicing, accounts payable, accounts receivable, income, and expenses. But that’s not all it should do. Below are some of the advanced features included in the best accounting software for small business.

Tax integration. Your accounting software should provide balance sheets, profit and loss reports, and any other customized reports you or your accountant require in order to file taxes. The top bookkeeping software even lets you photograph and save receipts using a mobile device so you have it all stored securely for tax time.

Payroll management. Payroll usually isn’t built into accounting software but is offered through integrations with third-party payroll and HR software. Once everything is set up, your software will be able to calculate and file your payroll, pay payroll taxes, pay with same-day direct deposit, and manage employee benefits.

Business insights. Online accounting software programs gather a lot of data about your business, so why not use all that data to your advantage? The best programs offer business insights and intelligence through user-friendly reports and dashboards.

Custom invoices and receipts. Remember, every interaction with customers and service providers is an opportunity to promote your brand. Some accounting programs let you create custom invoices and receipts, helping to make your brand more memorable.

Multi-user access. Depending on the size of your business, you may want to grant access to more than one person. The best accounting software programs offer plans for multiple users, including access for your accountant.

Support for mobile. You never know when you might need to capture or access data from a mobile device. Most of the big names in accounting software offer free iOS and Android apps.

Unlimited cloud storage. One of the benefits of using online accounting software is that all your data gets stored in the cloud, where capacity is virtually unlimited. 

Free support. If something goes wrong, then you want to know your software provider has your back. Premium subscriptions usually include a dedicated account team.

Scalability. Accounting software is perfect for the rapidly-expanding business that finds that manual entries no longer cut it. The sky’s the limit for your business–and so you need software that offers small business accounting services that scale with you.

User-friendly. Last, but not least, is user-friendliness. Your accounting and invoicing software should be easy enough for anyone on your team to learn how to use it within a couple of hours.

How Much Does Accounting Software Cost?

Like most software-as-a-service, the cost of online accounting software really depends on how many features you need and how many users need access. Pricing models can really vary when it comes to accounting software. Some providers charge a fixed per-month price with all or most of the features included, while others offer tiered pricing that gradually gets more expensive as more features are integrated.

Based on our research of the top providers, accounting software could cost anywhere from $12 to $300 per month. The cheapest subscriptions automate basic accounting functions such as tracking income and expenses, invoicing and accepting payments, managing cash flow, tracking sales and sales tax, and sending estimates. Integrating payroll costs extra—it’s built into some of the more expensive plans or costs another $4 - $10 per employee per month as an add-on. Advanced features like income tax return preparation almost always cost extra.

What is the Best Free Accounting Software?

Believe it or not, there is such thing as free accounting software–and we’re not just talking about Excel or Google Sheets. The biggest names in free accounting software include Wave, ZipBooks, and SlickPie. All of these are web-based accounting programs offering basic functions like managing accounts receivable, tracking expenses, and creating profit & loss and balance sheet statements. 

Free accounting software is a good stepping stone for sole proprietors and very small businesses looking to upgrade on spreadsheet programs like Excel and Google Sheets. They essentially let you do all the things Excel and Google Sheets could potentially do for you if you had the time to program all the necessary formulas yourself.

While free software is handy for doing basic things, the reality is it won’t give you anything close to the features offered by paid accounting software. If you need software that can carry out functions like managing payroll, tracking inventory, or handling tax preparation—then you’re going to need to pay for it.

Conclusion

If you can afford to automate administrative business tasks, then you probably should. Carrying out accounting tasks manually may be cheaper in the short-term, but you’ll quickly find it takes away time from growing your business and exposes you to the risk of potentially costly errors. The best accounting software grows with you, so you can start by automating just the core accounting tasks and then add on more complex tasks like payroll and tax reporting as you go. Once you begin using small business accounting software, you’ll quickly find yourself wondering why you ever did things manually.

QuickBooks at a Glance

Target Users: Entrepreneurs, freelancers, and businesses of all sizes seeking financial automation

Key Features: Invoicing, expense tracking, payroll, inventory management, budgeting, CRM tools, and financial reporting

New for July 2025: Smart search, AI-driven customer and accounting agents, anomaly detection, business feed, finance/project profitability tools, and enhanced CRM functionality including eSignatures

Integration: Compatible with over 750 third-party apps, including PayPal, Shopify, and Stripe

Accessibility: Available via web and mobile apps (iOS and Android), supporting remote access and real-time sync

Support: Tiered live support depending on plan, with extended access for Advanced users

QuickBooks Ease of Setup and Use

QuickBooks puts priority on its customer onboarding process. Those thinking about using the program for their accounting needs are encouraged to reach out to the QuickBooks sales team first which can be reached Monday to Friday from 9am to 5pm PT. Additionally, QuickBooks has put together comprehensive onboarding documentation that can guide clients through the setup process. QuickBooks is an intuitive and user-friendly platform to use. The web UI and mobile apps ensure that small businesses can update their accounts both from the office and while on the road.

QuickBooks Pricing and Plans

PackagePriceWho It’s For / Key FeaturesJuly 1, 2025 Feature Updates
Simple Start$38Best for solo entrepreneurs: invoicing, expense tracking, and general reports.

Smart search, business feed, progressive onboarding, tax readiness, basic automation

Essentials$75Best for small teams needing time tracking, bill management, and multi-user access.

Accounting & payments agent, auto-posting, customer CRM (referrals, tasks, appointments)

Plus$115Best for growing businesses managing projects, inventory, and job costing.

Customer agent (beta), AI reconciliation, anomaly detection, CRM with contracts, and eSignatures

Advanced$275Best for scaling businesses requiring advanced analytics, automation, and support.

Finance & projects agents (beta), KPI scorecard, enhanced automation, and reporting tools

What’s New in 2025

Beginning July 1, 2025, Intuit QuickBooks Online is launching a new suite of features across all tiers to enhance user experience and reduce manual tasks through AI-driven tools.

Simple Start now includes:

  • Smart Search: Customizable filters and column visibility for faster access to transactions, accounts, and help topics.

  • Business Feed: Consolidates updates from AI agents with actionable next steps and key highlights.

  • New Suite of Apps: Adds more utility to business workflows.

  • Progressive Onboarding: Streamlined setup experience for faster deployment.

  • Basic Automation & Tax Readiness Tools: Prepares users for smooth compliance and fewer manual entries.

Essentials adds:

  • Accounting & Payments Agent: Enhances real-time organization of books, facilitates faster payments with proactive recommendations.

  • Ready to Post / Auto-post & Collaboration Tools: Enables quicker transaction finalization and improved accountant communication.

  • Customer Hub (CRM): Centralizes referrals, feedback, scheduling, and relationship management with built-in task tracking.

Plus includes:

  • Customer Agent (beta): Scans emails to identify leads, drafts follow-ups, and logs status.

  • AI Reconciliation and Anomaly Detection (beta): Identifies transaction irregularities and streamlines bank reconciliations.

  • Insights Dashboard: Offers P&L and balance sheet intelligence to highlight trends and financial risks.

  • Expanded CRM Functions: Adds lead tracking, contract uploads with eSignatures, and a unified customer management interface.

Advanced upgrades with:

  • Finance & Projects Agents (beta): Provides profitability tracking and bookkeeping automation for project-based businesses.

  • KPI Scorecard: Visual dashboard for instant assessment of key performance indicators.

These updates are designed to reduce reliance on third-party tools and introduce AI-powered efficiency across accounting and client management processes. They reflect a significant shift toward automation and business intelligence within the QuickBooks ecosystem.

QuickBooks Features

Project Profitability Tracking

With QuickBooks, users can keep track of the profitability of every one of their projects. QuickBooks can pull in expense and cost of doing business (CODB) data in order to compute the level of profitability for each project underway. For project-based businesses, this feature allows them to easily identify cost overruns and keep within profitability targets.

Real Time Inventory Tracking

QuickBooks supports real time inventory tracking for organizations that sell online. Additionally, the QuickBooks website hosts an inventory tracker which is designed to prevent both understocking and overstocking. Customers can receive instant notifications about projected stock levels as soon as purchase orders (POs) are inputted to the system. On-demand reporting makes it easy for businesses to quickly identify their best-selling merchandise. Online sales reporting can sync with major Ecommerce retail platforms including Amazon, Etsy, and Shopify.

General Ledger and Expense Tracking

Expense Scanning

Users can capture expenses in QuickBooks by either scanning and uploading them directly into the platform or by emailing them to a unique address associated specifically with their account. After capturing receipts, users can categorize them in the system. Additionally, QuickBooks uses optical character recognition (OCR) technology to automatically determine the contents of scanned receipts including payment date, vendor, payment method used, and amount paid. Expenses can also be attached to invoices issued. This feature is useful for companies and freelancers that bill their clients for expenses incurred.

Billing and Invoicing

Bill Organization

QuickBooks supports invoice entry to keep track of accounts payable as well as accounts receivable. Using QuickBooks, companies can settle outstanding balances via credit or debit card as well as bank transfer. All payment options can be initiated from within the user area. All paid bills are recorded and tracked through the system. Additionally, users can connect their bank accounts to automatically track and categorize both inbound and outbound payments. The system also supports deferred bill payment in order to maximize cash flow.

Professional Invoicing

One of QuickBooks’s key features, of course, is the ability to create and send invoices. Using QuickBooks, users can:

  • Apply theme customizations so that the layout and color scheme of their invoices conforms to internal style and branding guidelines.
  • Configure recurring invoices. This is perfect for businesses that bill clients on retainer.
  • Add billable hours. In order to simplify the import of these, users can integrate QuickBooks with Google Calendar or TSheets and import hours that they have logged.

QuickBooks Integrations

QuickBooks supports a wide variety of integrations, allowing customers to do more with their online accounting platform by connecting it with other online services.

These include:

  • Calendar and time tracking apps: QuickBooks can integrate with Google Calendar and Tsheets in order to automatically import time logged on client accounts and bill that to clients.
  • There are also Ecommerce connectors. One example is the BigCommerce QuickBooks app, which allows companies to automatically generate documentation required for online sales.

QuickBooks Mobile Apps

QuickBooks has apps for both Android and iOS and these can be downloaded from the Google Play Store and the Apple App Store respectively. Only those features available in QuickBooks Online Simple Start are available in the app version. So, at the time of writing, customers on the Essentials, Plus, and Advanced plans will be unable to access their extra features from the mobile versions of their QuickBooks installations. Additionally the mobile versions can be used to access multiple accounts. Those that want to take and process payments directly through their mobile devices can do so with the QuickBooks mobile card reader. Customers can be invoiced directly through the app.

QuickBooks Customer Support

Need to reach out to the QuickBooks customer support team? Intuit maintains a comprehensive online troubleshooting section that it designed to help users resolve their own issues before reaching out to the team.

In the event that users are not able to resolve their question through the documentation, or the community forum, users can initiate a support discussion over live chat or by phone. The live chat option is accessible 6am to 6pm Monday to Friday (PT) and from 6am to 3pm on Saturday. The phone line is accessible from Monday to Friday 6am to 6pm and is closed on weekends.

Bottom Line

QuickBooks is a powerful invoicing and accounting system that is favored by small businesses all over the world. Its features include contractor expense tracking, project profitability reporting, and receipt capture by direct upload and email. There is no free tier, but paying users can choose the premium tier that best suits their needs

products.mainContent:
FreshBooks at a Glance

Best for: Small business owners that need an accounting system
Price range: From $21
Key features: Expenses tracking, estimates, multi-currency invoicing
Apps: iOS and Android apps
Integrations: Shopify, Squarespace, Zoom

FreshBooks Ease of Setup and Use

New users need to progress through a basic questionnaire to get set up on the system. The automatic onboarding program asks them for their name, business name, currency, and location. Once this information is registered and saved, any invoices that users create will be automatically populated with the correct details.

Using FreshBooks is very easy. Users simply click on areas of the invoice where they need to enter information. The style of the invoices created can be customized for color, or built around a template. In order to add a custom logo to the invoice or add line items, all users have to do is click on parts of the document.

FreshBooks Pricing and Plans

FreshBooks is available on 3 premium tiers. For especially large businesses that need to bill more than 500 clients, custom pricing is available through the Select Plan. The pricing per user is as follows:

TierLitePlusPremium
Pricing$21/month$38/month$65/month
Billable clientsUp to 5Up to 50Unlimited

Which tier users should sign up for really depends on how many billable clients they need. Additionally, the Plus and Premium tiers provide progressively more features—although all tiers thankfully include smartphone access through the iOS and Android apps, only Plus and Premium support mobile mileage tracking. Those on the Premium plan are able to invite their accountant to the system to simplify the process of compiling tax returns.

FreshBooks Features

FreshBooks contains sections for invoicing, account management, and time tracking. Users can also use the platform to send out estimates and to conduct double entry bookkeeping.

General Ledger and Expense Tracking

Tracking expenses with FreshBooks is as easy as creating invoices for clients. Users just begin typing the name of the merchant in order to populate the system with the information. Once a record has been created, it will set up a new account for that supplier so that any future payments can be recorded under the one account. Additionally, users can upload receipts directly from their computer. The expense can be marked as cost of goods sold and associated with client costs or marked as a recurrent expense. If it’s an expense that needs to be billed to a client for reimbursement, this can be marked too. Finally, expenses all have to be categorized by choosing from one of the drop down categories. This makes it easy for accounting teams to sort through expenses inputted and to account for them according to various deductibles.

Invoicing

Similar to creating expenses, setting up invoices in FreshBooks is as easy as clicking fillable fields on the document view screen. Users are also able to capture and log all invoices payable and a dashboard view can quickly compute the sum total of everything owed and owing. Clients that bill their customers on monthly retainers can also set up recurring invoices for a fixed amount which can be set to issue on a predetermined date or day every month.

Users can also connect their bank to the system in order to automatically capture inbound and outbound payments. FreshBooks supports more than 14,000 financial institutions including many major American banks including Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and Citibank. Paypal and American Express can also be integrated.

FreshBooks Integrations

FreshBooks integrates with a number of tools designed to make recording online accounting transactions even easier for users. These include:

  • Shopify: Shopify is a favorite go-to for Ecommerce retailers that want to set up online stores without the hassle. Using the FreshBooks-Shopify integration, storeowners can easily generate and send professional looking documentation.
  • Squarespace: Squarespace makes designing attractive looking websites incredibly easy. By integrating FreshBooks with Squarespace, store owners can automatically sync clients and orders to FreshBooks.
  • Zoom: FreshBooks users can easily attach meetings minutes from Zoom
  • Gusto: If users want to process payroll transactions using Gusto, then they can connect this information with FreshBooks in order to make sure that the transaction amounts are automatically synced and updated in the FreshBooks accounting system.

FreshBooks Mobile Apps

FreshBooks has apps for Android and iOS. These apps provide customers with the ability to create and import transactions, invoices, and expenses while on the go. For mobile mileage tracking, however, users will need to be on the Plus or Premium plan. One of the main advantages of using the mobile apps is that users can easily scan and append receipts to the system. At the time of writing, the Android app has a 4 and a half star rating on Google Play after more than 2,000 installations.

FreshBooks Customer Support

If users need to reach out for help, then they can do so by contacting FreshBooks’ support team. FreshBooks has clustered a variety of resources through its online support center which includes lots of helpful documentation for everything from invoicing through to creating expenses and generating reports.

The most effective way to get in touch with the team is by clicking on the ‘Submit Request’ button. Additionally, FreshBooks support can be reached by phone. The team is well known for its commitment to answer the phone within 2 rings. Finally, in addition to ticket-based and telephone support, users can send an email to the support address in order to receive help with the product.

Bottom Line

FreshBooks is an invoicing, expense tracking and accounting software that is perfect for business owners with a lot of clients to bill. The system can be scaled to support billing more than 500 clients but remains extremely user friendly with users only having to click on a fillable document to begin populating documents for clients.

The system can be scaled to support billing more than 500 clients but remains extremely user friendly with users only having to click on a fillable document to begin populating documents for clients.

What Is Sage Intacct?

Sage Intacct is a powerful cloud-based accounting software offering advanced financial management features tailored for mid-sized businesses and beyond. Sage Intacct has been a trusted choice for businesses needing scalability, automation, and robust reporting capabilities.

The software is ideal for organizations managing multi-entity financial structures, international operations, and diverse reporting needs. With AI integration, Sage Intacct simplifies repetitive tasks such as accounts payable and receivable, freeing up time for strategic financial planning.

Sage Intacct Features

Sage Intacct delivers a wide range of features that cater to the dynamic needs of growing businesses. Below are the highlights:

  • Intuitive user interface: Sage Intacct offers lots to explore and use, and I appreciate how it’s all organized. The interface is easy to navigate, and the graphic menus make it easy to select the function you need.

  • Dashboard: Intacct lets you build a reporting dashboard with pre-defined dimensions, allowing you to report on particular employees, departments, or items. You can further customize it with your own dimensions.

  • Reporting: Sage Intacct offers over 150 pre-built financial reports and fully customizable dashboards. The dimensions feature allows granular tracking, such as profitability by project or revenue by geography, all within clicks. You can easily summarize these or drill down to analyze information more closely.

  • Intelligent General Ledger: This feature combines AI-powered automation and dimensional reporting to provide real-time insights. It adapts to business-specific needs, simplifying reconciliations and reducing errors in multi-currency consolidations.

  • Accounts Payable and Receivable: AI streamlines invoice processing, automates recurring billing, and enhances cash flow visibility. This reduces manual entry errors and accelerates payment cycles

  • Communication tools: Exchange messages with colleagues through trackable conversations that are clearly linked to particular financial tasks, reports, or issues.

  • Customization options: Sage Intacct makes it easy to customize the wider platform beyond its core financial services. You can add custom fields, reports, tables, and dashboards, and create workflows and relationships to transfer data between them.

  • Integrations: With over 350 pre-built integrations, Sage Intacct connects seamlessly with CRMs like Salesforce, payroll systems, and industry-specific solutions. Its open APIs also enable custom integration setups.

How to Get Started With Sage Intacct

Getting started with Sage Intacct is a guided process:

  1. Demo and Consultation: Schedule a demo to explore its capabilities.
  2. Implementation: Once you’re ready to start, you’ll sign up for your business account with the support of Sage's professional services team (You can’t set up the service independently).
  3. Training and Onboarding: Access Sage University for comprehensive training.
  4. Go live in 91 Days: Typical implementations, including integrations, are completed within three to six months.

How Sage Intacct Works

Sage Intacct is a feature-rich accounting platform you can configure to suit your business. You don’t need coding knowledge to set up Intacct and use the customization options. All you need to do is choose your desired settings and adjust the fields and dimensions.

Since Sage Intacct offers so many features, there’s much to learn. It’s a good idea to set aside some time to review the Intacct product brochure, training resources, walkthroughs, and guides on the Sage website to familiarize yourself with the platform.

The first step in implementation is setting up the core accounting features. These include the Intelligent General Ledger, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and Initial Reporting. For these to run, you must add the key details about your business (e.g., current income and outgoings) and your customers (e.g., their addresses and contact names). You’ll also need to import any pre-existing invoices and bills and set up any recurring payments or subscriptions.

You can also set up a range of product integrations by selecting them from the Sage Intacct Marketplace. This can save you significant time and effort. For example, you can integrate with your CRM software, import existing information, and avoid having to create brand-new customer profiles.

Once your account is up and running, you can start selecting and editing the dashboards and reports you need to understand what’s happening in your business.

Sage Intacct Customer Service

Designated Support Users

It's firstly important to note that only designated support users, such as administrators, IT contacts, or project managers authorized by your company, can interact directly with Sage Intacct Support. These users handle tasks like resolving login issues, product questions, and troubleshooting. They can open support cases, call customer service, and log into the Sage Intacct Community for further resources.

If you're an Intacct partner, you can call Support or log a support case directly.

Self-Service Resources

Sage Intacct provides several self-service tools to resolve issues independently before contacting support. The Help Center offers contextual assistance directly from any Intacct page and allows users to search for detailed guides, troubleshooting tips, and feature information. The Sage Intacct Community features a knowledge base with over 10,000 articles and provides a platform to ask questions and receive answers from peers and product experts. Additionally, Sage University delivers interactive training courses to help users gain proficiency in the platform.

Customer Support Contact Details

For direct assistance, Sage Intacct Customer Support operates Monday through Friday, 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM local time, with after-hours support available for high-priority issues.

Contact Numbers by Region:

  • North America: (800) 628-6583
  • United Kingdom: +44 191 479 5911
  • Australia: +61 1300 729 330
  • South Africa: +27 (0)11 304 3220
  • France: 01 70 73 16 40
  • Germany: +49 69 500076297

Alternatively, you can log a support case anytime from your admin account.

Additionally, you’ll receive a dedicated Account Manager when you use Sage Intacct. You can contact them directly for queries and support.

Is Sage Intacct Safe and Reliable?

Sage monitors its cloud servers 24/7 and uses web application firewalls, traffic inspection, serverless and container security, and secure back-ups to ensure your data stays safe.

The company protects your data in transit using Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol and encrypts the data at rest, too. You can also set up 2FA (two-factor authentication) to log into your account, further increasing security.

How to Cancel or Pause a Sage Intacct Subscription

If you decide Sage Intacct is no longer the right fit for your business, canceling your subscription is straightforward. However, it's important to note that data access is revoked immediately upon cancellation, so be sure to save any essential information beforehand, such as Balance Sheets, Profit and Loss statements, and Trial Balances.

Steps to Cancel Your Subscription:

  1. Access Your Account Settings:
    In the upper-right corner of your Sage Intacct account, select your business name and click Manage Business Account.

  2. Manage Your Subscription:
    Navigate to the Subscription and Invoices section and select Manage my Subscription.

  3. Choose and Cancel:
    From your list of subscriptions, select the one you wish to cancel and click Cancel my Subscription. Provide a reason for cancellation when prompted.

  4. Await Confirmation:
    Your cancellation request will be processed by Sage’s accounting team, and you’ll be notified once the account has been officially canceled.

Important Notes:

Final Payment Policy:
Sage operates on a monthly billing cycle. If you cancel:

  • On or before the 16th of the month, your current month’s invoice will still be due.
  • After the 16th but before the 1st of the following month, no additional payment will be required, as you’ve already paid for the full month.

Reactivation:
You can reinstate your account and reactivate the service by submitting a written request. This request must come from the registered business owner or the individual who originally set up the account.

Is There a Sage Intacct App?

Currently, there isn't a dedicated Sage Intacct mobile app for general use. However, users can access the platform through a web browser on any smartphone, desktop, laptop, or tablet. Additionally, there is a mobile app specifically designed for timesheet management, allowing users to enter time from anywhere, which can help streamline the process of tracking hours worked.

Sage Intacct Pricing

products.mainContent:
HR Features

As previously mentioned, Gusto tries its hardest to “treat people like people, not ID numbers.” It does this by offering an easy platform for managers to work with (taking much of the burden and stress off of their shoulders) and a benefits-laden program for employees to enjoy (making workers happier to work for you!) These are some of the features we really liked from Gusto’s feature menu:

Payroll

Most HR software offers payroll services, and Gusto is no different. What does make it stand out is the unlimited payroll option. This service allows users to pay employees any time they want for no additional fees. There is no need to wait until the scheduled payment cycle arrives. Gusto payroll lets you make off-cycle payments, award bonuses, and factor in one-time workers without a hassle. Canceling payments is also easier with Gusto than most other sites.

Everything customers need is also seamlessly integrated with Gusto’s payroll - including health insurance, 401(k), workers’ comp, time tracking, PTO, etc - so you can avoid manual entering of data and just need to review and approve. For example, Gusto recently launched Time Kiosk, which enables employees to clock in and out securely from a centralized station in just a few seconds. It’s also seamlessly integrated with Gusto’s payroll, so you never need to track time manually again. Boost your efficiency and accuracy with employee hours automatically syncing when you run payroll.

Gusto also offers peace of mind on taxes and compliance. It tracks ever-changing laws and regulations and calculates the impact, so customers don’t have to worry. Employee I9s, W2s, and contractor 1099s are stored and organized online for quick access. State tax registration in all 50 states makes it easy for customers to hire and pay employees across state lines.

Benefits

Gusto helps you offer your team affordable health and financial benefits - making your company a better place to work and helping you attract and retain the right talent.

It provides health benefits (medical, dental, vision), financial benefits (401(k), HSA, FSA, 529), and extras (commuter, workers compensation). It automates benefits deductions with payroll to reduce manual errors and provide live support with licensed advisors.

With 9,000+ health insurance plans, 30+ carriers, and licensed advisors, Gusto can help customers find the right plan for their budget. For customers who already have health benefits, they can easily move their existing insurance broker to Gusto.

HR Tools

Gusto can help you make your dream team a reality with tools for hiring, onboarding, and talent development.

You can streamline hiring by managing applicants in one place and creating and sharing job postings on 100+ of the top job sites, including LinkedIn and Indeed.

With a customizable onboarding checklist and digital tools for paperwork, you can quickly onboard new staff. You or a manager can just click a button to automatically onboard the new employee. Then, the system sends all of the necessary contracts, tax forms, and paperwork to the new recruit to sign and send back. It’s faster and more efficient than ever.

With Gusto, you can develop your employees with tools for Performance Reviews, Goal Tracking, Employee Pulse Surveys, and a Learning Management System.

For more complex needs, Gusto provides a robust suite of software integrations for hiring, onboarding, and performance management to keep all your data in one place.

Gusto provides an HR Resource Center with guidance and templates for compliance, as well as professionals to keep you informed around changing HR requirements.

The ability to hire and manage talent from around the world, compliantly

Recently, Gusto announced the launch of Gusto Global, an Employer of Record (EOR) solution enabling businesses to hire full-time employees worldwide, without cutting compliance corners. Powered by Remote, Gusto Global enables you to hire, pay, and manage talent through Gusto’s all-in-one platform and quickly run payroll for your whole team, whether in the U.S. or overseas, contract, or full-time. Having one platform for all your staff helps you keep your finances running smoothly without worrying about managing unconnected systems and tools.

What’s also critical is Gusto Global enables you to pay your team compliantly. One of the most challenging parts of hiring international employees is ensuring you maintain compliance. Failing compliance in another country can mean paying hefty fines or no longer being allowed to operate in that country. For example, in Canada, fines for misclassifying employees can range between $50,000 to $500,000. In Australia, similar violations can cost $80,000 each. But with Gusto, you’ll have peace of mind about complying with all foreign laws and regulations in the countries where Gusto Global is available.

Gusto Global is available in beta in Canada now, and will be available in additional countries soon. Remote operates in more than 75 countries around the world.

However, if you’re not ready to hire full-time international staff, and if you’d rather work with international contractors or freelancers, Gusto has you covered there too. Gusto allows you to pay international contractors in more than 120 countries around the world with just a few clicks, again all through its all-in-one platform.

Accounting and Time Management

In addition to Gusto’s native time tracking and Time Kiosk solutions, Gusto also offers 3rd party time tracking integrations, such as Deputy and Homebase, so you can easily see which employees are taking their work seriously (combine that with the talent, attendance, and task management features, and you can get a really clear picture of employee productivity). Additionally, Gusto syncs with QuickBooks, Xero, TSheets, and other time sheets, so your hours are instantly updated and added to the payments system. Tax management features ensure that your books are always handled properly according to state and federal legislation, and Gusto will even update your taxes according to the latest reforms and regulations.

Records and Reports

Gusto reports are simple for even the most non-technical employee. Fields are customizable, and you can create, manage, and print several types of reports including payroll reports, individual employee productivity charts or team reports, timesheets, employee surveys (anonymous or by name), and new hire reports.

Usability

The modern online user interface makes adding and updating information easy. What’s more, once you’ve set up your schedules, settings, and preferences, Gusto HR software takes care of most of the work automatically. This way, you don’t have to keep going back to update or manually set things in motion.

Gusto is mobile-optimized, so you can log directly onto the website from your mobile device without the added step of downloading an app. The mobile site has all of the same functionality, features, and navigation as the regular desktop site with exactly the same look, feel, and processing for a seamless experience.

For employees of your business, Gusto offers a free mobile app called Gusto Wallet. It enables your employees to track, save, and access their hard-earned money. Employees can set budgets and save automatically while tracking their paychecks and tax documents.

Gusto has strong layers of security on its site, so users might not appreciate the 2-step authentication, but it is really the best way to keep your organization and business information secure. As a side note, Gusto also provides thorough security for all of its data centers, including biometric and iris scanner locks, surveillance cameras that are monitored 24/7, and onsite security staff.

Gusto Customer Support

The entire look and feel of the site is friendly, open, honest, and clear, which makes for a better, quality user experience right from the start. Gusto continues with the same attitude by hiring and training professional customer support staff to field all of its customer relations and questions. Every experience we had with Gusto’s customer service was a positive one, and you will find the same results from an online search of its reviews.

Gusto recently expanded its customer support hours. Here are their hours of operation below:

Callback hours

  • Basic support (Simple plan): 9am - 4pm PT
  • Full support (Plus, Plus +, and Premium plans): 7am - 4pm PT
  • VIP Accountant Partner: 7am - 4pm PT

Chat hours

  • Standard hours: 7am - 4pm PT

Pricing & Special Offers

Recognizing the challenges and potential financial pitfalls of manual payroll processing, Gusto stands out as a cost-effective solution for small business owners. Many entrepreneurs in the U.S. still tackle payroll by hand, a risky approach that often results in costly mistakes and thousands of dollars in IRS fees each year.

Gusto addresses this issue head-on, offering an automated, reliable, and user-friendly service that not only corrects existing payroll issues but also prevents future errors. By choosing Gusto, businesses are making a smart long-term investment. The cost of utilizing Gusto’s services is consistently lower than the hefty fees and penalties associated with manual payroll errors.

When it comes to pricing, Gusto ensures affordability and transparency. Even with its highly competitive rates, such as the $40 per month plus $6 per user on Gusto’s Simple Plan, you receive a comprehensive package of services.

This plan includes automatic tax filing, unlimited payrolls, diverse pay rates and schedules, multi-state payroll capabilities, time off tracking, tax form amendments, and expedited payroll services when applicable.

Especially for startups and SMBs, this Simple package offers an economical yet feature-rich option, ensuring that businesses of all sizes have access to essential services like unlimited payrolls, tax filing, unemployment insurance, extensive reports, health benefits, and unwavering customer support.

Gusto also offers a free trial, something you won’t find with most other HR software providers. This is a serious advantage as you can test drive the software without any commitment. You also won’t have to pay any setup fees or end-of-the-year W2 filing with this company.

Bottom Line

Providing a wide range of helpful features, offering useful and clear information directly on its website, and delivering more services than you could imagine, Gusto is a pleasure to work with. Combine that with the full range of services and a surprisingly affordable price tag, and this company quickly shoots to the top of the charts. With a free trial, you can’t go wrong.

Striven Ease of Setup and Use

To get started with Striven, you can take the platform for a test drive, with free access to a test environment, for seven days. You need only supply your name and email address, and no credit card details are required.

Alternatively, you can connect one-on-one with a business analyst from Striven to discuss your business requirements and see a live demo. The business analyst will set you up with a 30-day free account so you can familiarize yourself with the platform before committing to a purchase.

While most people find the interface intuitive and easy to navigate, some users have found that the large number of functions available on the Striven system can make it confusing for new users. However, the Striven interface is completely customizable and can be configured to only display the lists, tasks, and projects that you need.

In addition to live chat and phone support from 8am-8pm EST, Striven provides comprehensive support and advice, including walkthroughs, videos, webinars, and a large collection of user guides. Guides cover initial setup, productivity tools, emails, campaigns, workflows, and more.

Striven Features

Striven offers a comprehensive suite of tools that includes accounting, customer relationship management (CRM), project management, inventory control, and human resources (HR) in one system.

General Ledger and Expense Tracking

Striven enables you to manage budget planning, bank integration, ledger accounting, and more. You can use Striven to create and manage multiple general ledger accounts within the same system in order to keep track of your expenses and financial transactions. The general ledger accounts can be customized to suit the particular needs of your business. You can also generate real-time reports on cash flows and financial performance.

Inventory Management

Striven's inventory management tools give you a clear insight into the current state of your inventory so that you can stay organized and on top of your stock levels. You can create bill of material lists and efficiently maintain and update your records. Striven also enables you to estimate the cost of materials quickly, either by inputting pre-defined data or manually entering it.

Billing and Invoicing

Billing and invoicing features make it easy to create invoices, track payments, and generate reports on your billing activities. Customers can pay their invoices online through Striven's Customer Portal. The portal allows customers to securely upload payment information, view their outstanding balance, and make payments.

CRM

Striven's CRM helps businesses build and maintain relationships with their customers. Striven automates customer communication, such as automatic emails, monthly statements, and customized reminders. It also powers sales funnels from start to finish and automatically assesses the probability and profitability of each lead. With real-time reports and visual dashboards, you can analyze business metrics and get an accurate picture of your sales pipeline from prospect to close.

Project Management

Striven’s project management tool allows you to keep track of projects, tasks, and deadlines. You can assign tasks to team members and get notifications when they’re completed. With an array of customizable views, you can monitor your team's progress on specific projects or analyze overall performance.

Striven offers features that make collaborating with colleagues effortless. Track and manage appointments, view coworker conflicts for meeting times and locations, get alerts and reminders for meetings, view peer calendars, and request meetings with colleagues, customers, and vendors. Plus, you can integrate with Google Calendar to sync up with your contacts.

HR

Striven’s HR tools enable you to manage and communicate with both potential candidates and your existing workforce. This includes creating job postings, recruiting applicants, scheduling interviews, tracking employee benefits and salary history, and sharing news and announcements in a real-time feed. You’ll also be able to centralize document storage and HR records within the system for easy access.

Productivity Tools

Efficiency is the key to success when it comes to running a business. Striven makes it easy to stay organized and productive with productivity tools like chat, a resource navigator, a smart calendar, a company newsfeed, and employee feedback.

These features streamline daily tasks and improve collaboration between teams, so everyone can work together more effectively. For example, you can calculate the average response and resolution times for employees’ completed tasks, which is useful if you have Service-Level Agreements with customers. Striven's Document Management feature stores and shares important documents online in a secure environment.

Portals

Striven offers three different portals: customer, vendor, and applicant portals. All three provide secure, real-time access to important information and resources. The customer portal allows customers to manage their accounts, pay invoices, submit tasks and view their work history. The vendor portal enables vendors to send PO requests quickly and securely. Lastly, the applicant portal provides a convenient way for applicants to apply for jobs and check the status of their applications.

With these portals, your customers and vendors can self-serve when they need information or want to make changes to their accounts. Striven enables third parties to access the information they need when they need it. Portals come at an additional cost on top of the usual pricing plan.

Striven Integrations

Striven integrates with multiple other applications. These include the following.

  • Gmail

  • Google Calendar

  • Authorize.net—accept online payments through Authorize.net’s gateway

  • ShipStation—status updates on sales, orders, and fulfillment

  • Twilio—automated SMS notifications

  • Email Relay—enable emails from the Striven system to come from your company’s server

  • APIs—connect Striven to outside sources to send and receive data

Striven Mobile Apps

Striven doesn’t offer a mobile app to users. The platform is designed to be used on desktop and laptop computers for maximum efficiency. Though, it's worth noting that Striven is a cloud-based system and is fully mobile-responsive for people who work on mobile devices in the field.

Striven Customer Support

You can contact Striven’s customer support team by phone, via online chat, or by submitting an online ticket. Alternatively, you can schedule a support call with one of its customer service representatives. The customer support team is available 8am-8pm ET, Monday to Friday. The customer service team scores highly in user reviews, with 5 stars on Google, 4.8 on Capterra, and 4.5 on G2.

There’s a wide selection of information available online, too, including user guides, blog articles, and training videos.

Bottom Line

Striven offers an all-in-one solution to help businesses streamline operations and bring together multiple business requirements in a single system. It includes an integrated suite of business software solutions, including accounting, CRM, inventory management, and HR software. With the addition of Striven's secure real-time portals, customers, vendors, and applicants can self-serve when they need information or want to make changes to their accounts.

These features provide a comprehensive platform that could make managing your business more accessible and more efficient. There’s little to lose when you can set up a free seven-day or 30-day trial to see if Striven is the right choice for your business.

1-800Accountant Ease of Setup and Use

Getting started with 1-800Accountant involves following an onboarding/signup section with one of their expert account managers. In order to go through this process, users need to click on the online signup widget which then redirects towards a calendar booking form.

After scheduling a call with one of 1-800Accountant’s tax planning experts, users will be invited to actually sign up for an account on the platform.

1-800Accountant offers three main pricing plans as well as one enterprise-only plan for companies that meet the following criteria:

  • More than $1 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR)
  • More than 5 employees

Therefore, most small to medium-sized organizations will opt for one of the bottom three plans. Their pricing and what they include is given in the following table:

One of the most basic accounting services required by businesses is tax preparation and 1-800Accountant’s team of fully licensed CPAs can assist in this respect.

Small Business Payroll

1-800Accountant’s payroll experts work to make sure that the business stays IRS-compliant throughout the payment cycle. Automated payment systems also ensure that the payment process runs seamlessly every time.

Auditing

1-800Accountant offers an audit protection service designed to help prepare the business in the event that an audit notice is received. The service involves ensuring that all relevant paperwork is in order so that the business will be in maximum compliance with the dictates of the IRS.

Tax Advice

If you’re searching for a responsive and proactive accountancy partner that will be able to provide answers for all your critical taxation questions, then the tax advice that 1-800Accountant includes as part of its package may prove invaluable to you.

There is no limit on the questions you can ask and both enrolled agents (EAs) and CPAs are available to field questions. Clients also get access to a resource center designed to keep them up to date on the latest developments in the world of taxation and compliance.

This streamlines the process of quickly capturing the information that needs to be added in order to prepare accounts.

Every client that signs up for a package also receives a dedicated accountant — so there is continuity in the relationship. Additionally, the website features an online chatbot which can help to quickly direct users’ queries towards the most appropriate resource.

Bottom Line

If you’re a small business that is interested in outsourcing your bookkeeping and accountancy needs, then 1-800Accountant provides a variety of tiers and one of them might be a good fit for your requirements. Zoho Billing Ease of Setup and Use

Zoho Billing offers a straightforward setup and onboarding process. You simply select a plan, create an account, and sign in to your dashboard. Because it’s a cloud-based offering, there is no software to download or install—everything is online.

If you’re using Zoho Billing for the first time, the software will take you through a step-by-step onboarding process. You’ll be able to customize the platform according to your organization’s needs, connect any external accounts, and input tax details.

The program sports an intuitive and streamlined dashboard, where you can get an at-a-glance look at your organization's financial metrics. For a more detailed view, Zoho Billing keeps tabs on your invoice, expense, sales, and banking history. The platform also allows you to track time spent on projects, automate certain tasks, and integrate with payroll and inventory management providers

You can even invite other users to the platform—so if you have an accountant or a part-time bookkeeper, you can add them, too. In addition, you can create custom roles with unique permissions so that your staff only get access to what they need.

Zoho Billing Features

Zoho Billing is a comprehensive accounting platform that features expense tracking, budgeting, and payment capabilities.

General Ledger and Expense Tracking

All businesses using Zoho Billing can set up a general ledger, chart of accounts, and journals—and can track and categorize expenses by linking their credit card and bank accounts. Subscribers to the Professional plan gain access to multi-currency and recurring billing features, while Premium plan users can benefit from budgeting and project costing functions.

Inventory Management

If your business has complex inventory tracking needs, you can integrate Zoho Billing with Zoho Inventory to unlock access to more sophisticated offerings, such as item management, backorder tracking, inventory analytics, and vendor relationship management.

Billing and Invoicing

All Zoho Billing plans, including the free version, have access to invoicing and bill pay. Clients can pay directly using the built-in invoicing feature, though you can integrate with other payment processors, such as Stripe or PayPal, for more flexibility.

Subscribers to the Professional and Premium plans also receive access to project management, time tracking, job costing, and custom reporting—allowing business owners to get a more granular understanding of a project’s risks and profitability.

However, Zoho Billing doesn’t come with payroll. For that, you’ll need to integrate with Zoho Payroll, which is currently available only in California, Texas, Florida, and New York.

Zoho Billing Customer Support

products.mainContent:
Xero at a Glance

Best for

Small and medium-sized businesses

Price range

$12—$65 a month

Key features

Bookkeeping tools

Journal entries

Audit trails

Invoice customization

Financial statements

Custom reporting

Workflow capability with user, role and access management

Apps

Offers three Android and iOS apps. One is a mobile app, the second is an employee cost reimbursement app, and the third is for project management.

Integrations

Xero has close integrations with HubDoc. HubDoc is compatible with QuickBooks Online and Bill.com.


Xero Ease of Setup and Use

Using its direct conversion tool, Xero makes it easy to import records, transactions, and other information from QuickBooks Online. You can also import CSV or TXT-formatted files, such as contacts, inventory items, invoices, etc.

If you're new to Xero, you may utilize the site's comprehensive setup page to get started. An introduction video outlines the initial steps for establishing the website for your own business. You can put them into practice by following the detailed instructions

This involves linking your bank accounts, examining Xero's transaction categories, and managing your invoices. Some introductory information explains these functions, followed by connections to pages where you can experiment with example data or begin inputting your own.

Xero’s setup tool is superior to what most rivals provide, as it introduces you to accounting principles like the Chart of Accounts early on. This can be advantageous to first-time users, who will better understand Xero workflows after completing the setup process.

However, the lengthy introduction may discourage better-oriented customers who wish to begin working immediately. Thankfully, if you want, you can hide these steps and return to them later.

Overall, Xero’s layout and interfaces are neat and accessible for people even without any accounting experience. The user interface centralizes all of the user’s account information on a dashboard. The dashboard itself is customizable and provides a snapshot of the financial status at one glance.

Xero Pricing and Plans

Xero follows a software as a service (SaaS) model with subscriptions based on the type and number of company entities managed by the user. After a 30-day free trial, Xero is available in three pricing tiers.

Xero Early ($12 per month) has unlimited bank transaction reconciliation but is restricted to 20 invoices and quotes and five bills.

Xero Growing ($34 per month), which is the most popular plan, includes limitless billing and invoicing estimates and invoices.

Only Xero Established ($65 per month) has support for several currencies and allows for tracking of projects and claiming expenses. It also supports all the functions offered by Xero Early and Growing.

All plans also include Hubdoc integration.

While Xero’s Established plan targets corporations with more than 100 employees, larger businesses may still face some trouble adapting the Xero features for their business model if they make use of several payment processing options or multiple bank accounts.

Overall, Xero’s plans are best suited for startups and small-to-medium-sized businesses.

Xero Features

Ever since its inception, Xero has improved and continually added more new features to enhance its usability and functionality. Key features include the following.

General ledger and expense tracking

Xero enables users to track and record all spending. The mobile app features a receipt scanner that makes it simple to post receipts, and, if the receipt is digital, you can import it.

Xero users can also save supplier, product, and customer information to account for each expense properly.

Through the "accounts/transactions," "insights," and "monthly review" sections, Xero helps small companies monitor outgoing spending. These sections allow you to filter reports by dates and spending categories.

Inventory Management

One huge advantage Xero has over its competitors is its robust inventory management tool. With this feature, you can keep track of what’s in stock and populate invoices and orders with items you buy and sell.

Using Xero’s inventory management system, you can track up to 4,000 finished items. Other features enable you to do the following.

  • Look up the number of items on hand and available to sell

  • See the total value of the stock on hand for any item

  • See the best-selling and worst-selling items

  • See the most profitable and least profitable lines, etc.

Billing and Invoicing

Xero provides customized invoice templates that can be modified to contain your company's logo, items, prices, and other information. You can also save your templates for later use.

You can allow online payments for your invoices. If you pick this option, consumers will be able to pay using their bank account, Amex, Visa, Discover, or Mastercard through the invoice.

A few years ago, Xero developed a new invoice form. This new form expedites the invoicing process for customers due to its intelligent simplicity and visual appeal. It seems more modern and is less crowded than earlier versions, and it automatically saves your work every few seconds.

Xero can send invoices to your clients automatically using the information you provide. The software has the capability to issue reminders to clients whose invoices remain unpaid past the due date.

For payroll features, third-party integration is required. All three plans have an optional add-on with Gusto, a popular payroll application, for $39 per month and $6 per month per person.

Xero Integrations

Xero integrates with some powerful tools and applications, including the following.

  • Spendesk

  • Receipt Bank

  • BigCommerce

  • Timely

  • Stripe

  • PayPal


And the list goes on. You can have a look at Xero’s App store to check out all the available apps and integrations that Xero offers now.

Xero Mobile Apps

Three apps are available from Xero, each with an Android and iOS version.

The first application delivers a condensed version of the website's content. It’s divided into four sections: Dashboard, Sales, Purchases, and Contacts. The dashboard presents account balances, sales and buy totals, monthly profit, and cash in/out chart.

In the Sales section, you may examine and create new invoices and quotations, while the Purchases button allows you to examine bills, purchase orders, and costs and manually produce bills and receipts.

The second mobile app, Xero Expenditures, is for workers who must submit reimbursable expenses but do not require main site access. This software allows employees to photograph receipts using their smartphones. Then, Xero extracts information from the receipts and populates it into the browser-based expense forms.

The third app, Xero Projects, allows you to examine ongoing projects and monitor tasks, time, expected costs, spending, and locations. This app is meant for employees who contribute to projects but do not require full access to Xero.

Xero Customer Support

The importance of support for small company accounting website users cannot be overstated. The worldwide network of advisers for Xero comprises application specialists that can assist small companies. Xero’s support team is available online for all its users 24/7.

There are no specific phone numbers provided for customer support on the website. However, the team responds quickly to email support. After getting in touch through email, users can also schedule a time slot for a chat.

The site's online documentation is superior, providing detailed instructions for using the product. This includes a vast database of self-help resources like blogs, video lessons and podcasts.

Xero has received 5/5 from multiple users and online communities in customer support and expert guidance.

Bottom Line

Xero is a cloud-based accounting solution designed for small enterprises. It provides features for spending management, accounting, and billing. Its mobile app is user friendly and can perform all the functions commonly performed on the website.

Xero includes excellent facilities for account reconciliation, project monitoring, and managing sales and buying transactions. Though it’s not highly scalable, recent enhancements to its setup procedure and company overviews make it a decent option for small firms.
products.verdict: Xero is a cloud-based accounting solution designed for small enterprises. It provides features for spending management, accounting, and billing. Its mobile app is user friendly and can perform all the functions commonly performed on the website.

articles.mainContent:
As a financial expert, I've spent years working with various personal finance software, and while Quicken has long been a trusted name in the industry, it’s not the only option available.

Whether you’re searching for a more intuitive interface, better budgeting tools, or advanced investment tracking features, there are a variety of accounting software alternatives that might suit you better.

Based on my extensive research and hands-on testing, I’ve identified five standout options that truly redefine personal finance management. These tools address common financial challenges, making it easier for you to take control of your budget, savings, and investments.

Join me as we explore these Quicken alternatives and discover how they can transform the way you manage your money.

» Need some help? Here's how to choose the right accounting software.

Our 5 Best Quicken Alternatives in 2026:

  • Oracle Netsuite - Best Quicken alternative overall
  • Fresh Books - Best for freelancers and solopreneurs
  • Zoho Books - Best for small to medium-sized businesses (SMBs)
  • 1-800Accountant - Best for expert tax and financial advice
  • Patriot Software - Best for integrated HR and accounting software

A Closer Look at the Best Quicken Alternatives in 2026

1. Oracle Netsuite

Experience comprehensive business management with a cloud-based ERP

  • Best for - Scalable cloud-based solutions
  • Price range - Pricing on request
  • Free trial - No

Oracle NetSuite's accounting software offers practical features for everyday business needs. It automatically tracks your income and expenses, creating real-time financial reports you can access anytime. This means you can quickly check your cash flow, profit margins, and budget status without waiting for month-end closings.

The system also simplifies tax preparation by organizing your financial data annually. It can handle multiple currencies and automate invoice creation and payment reminders if you do business globally. For growing businesses, NetSuite scales easily, allowing you to add users or modules for inventory management, payroll, or advanced reporting.

What Makes Oracle Netsuite a Good Alternative to Quicken?

It lets me manage finances for multiple locations all in one place, which Quicken can't do. NetSuite also handles complex billing and long-term contracts better, and its financial reports are more detailed and customizable. I can see real-time data on easy-to-use dashboards, giving me a clearer picture of my business's financial health.

Pros

  • Free NetSuite license for accounting professionals
  • Seamless integration with other tools
  • Real-time metrics and role-based dashboards

Cons

  • No free trial available
  • The initial setup can be overwhelming

2. FreshBooks

Simplified accounting for small businesses

  • Best for - 30-day free trial of its fully cloud-hosted accounting software
  • Price - From $19/month
  • Free trial - Yes

FreshBooks caters to small businesses, freelancers, and solopreneurs with its user-friendly accounting platform. The interface is intuitive, automating time-consuming tasks like invoicing and expense tracking. It lets you easily streamline your whole routine.

It also offers accounting features like double-entry reporting without breaking the bank. FreshBooks hits the sweet spot if you want to manage your finances efficiently without wrestling with complicated software.

What Makes Fresh Books a Good Alternative to Quicken?

Unlike Quicken, which can be complex and overwhelming for small business owners, FreshBooks offers a simpler, more user-friendly experience. Its focus on invoicing, expense tracking, and payment processing makes it ideal for basic accounting features without the complexity of full-scale accounting software.

Pros

  • 30-day money-back guarantee
  • Integrates with 100+ apps
  • Double-entry accounting reports feature

Cons

  • Limited scope for customization
  • Extra cost per month to add an additional team member

3. Zoho Books

Automate, collaborate and go global with Zoho Books

  • Best for - Free plan
  • Price - From $20/month
  • Free trial or free version - Yes

Zoho Books is a cloud accounting solution with a user-friendly interface. It simplifies invoicing, inventory management, and project tracking. A major draw is the free plan, which gives users essential accounting tools without costly subscriptions.

For growing businesses, paid tiers unlock advanced features like purchase approvals, vendor portals, and custom modules. Zoho Books offers an intuitive mobile app for on-the-go accounting. It also provides multi-channel support, including phone and chat assistance, plus an extensive knowledge base.

What Makes Zoho Books a Good Alternative to Quicken?

Unlike Quicken, which focuses primarily on personal finance, Zoho Books solves business needs. It gives you a more comprehensive set of invoicing, inventory management, and project tracking features. Its cloud-based platform also provides greater accessibility and collaboration for businesses.

Pros

  • Customizable invoicing templates
  • Multi-currency support
  • Automated bank reconciliation saves time and improves accuracy

Cons

  • Premium plan limited to 10 users
  • Advanced inventory features only available in higher-tier plans

4. 1-800Accountant

Empower your business with tailored accounting expertise and flat-rate support

  • Best for - Personalized tax advice and planning
  • Price - From $179/month billed annually
  • Free trial or free version - Yes

1-800Accountant comes with a comprehensive suite of accounting services handled by expert professionals. This includes bookkeeping, tax prep, payroll, and even entity formation for new businesses. Plus, its mobile app provides convenient remote access to your accounts.

For more advanced needs, the Enterprise plan unlocks features like in-depth financial reporting and dedicated bookkeeping services. While some functionality is reserved for top tiers, 1-800Accountant provides reliable, full-service accounting support from seasoned pros.

What Makes 1-800Accountant a Good Alternative to Quicken?

Quicken focuses on personal finance, but 1-800Accountant caters to small businesses. It offers a dedicated accountant, year-round tax advice, and proactive tax planning. With flat-rate pricing and customizable packages, you can access expertise to help you navigate complex tax forms and changing regulations while focusing on growing your business.

Pros

  • 4.4/5 star Trustpilot rating
  • 30-day money-back guarantee
  • Manages multiple business entities

Cons

  • Lacks a monthly subscription option
  • Financial reports and bookkeeping services only available in Enterprise plan

5. Patriot Software

Affordable accounting and payroll software for small businesses

  • Best for - Affordable accounting and payroll solutions
  • Price - From $20/month
  • Free trial or free version - Yes

Patriot Software provides straightforward, affordable accounting and payroll for small businesses. The company keeps it simple with unlimited payroll runs, accurate tax calculations, and free direct deposit or check printing options. Having integrated HR software is a nice perk, too.

It offers transparent pricing and quality customer service, which is evident in its 4.9/5 star Trustpilot rating. If you're a small business owner looking to streamline accounting and payroll without complications, this could be the no-fuss solution you need.

What Makes Patriot Software a Good Alternative to Quicken?

Unlike Quicken's personal finance focus, Patriot Software is built specifically for small businesses. It integrates accounting, payroll, and HR functions into one platform. You also get software unlimited vendor payments, 1099 creation, and a free contractor portal. Plus, its user-based permissions and departmental tracking also offer greater flexibility for growing companies.

Pros

  • Automated bank transaction imports to save time on data entry
  • Free 30-day trial
  • Unlimited payroll runs

Cons

  • No international payroll support
  • Limited integration features

What to Look For in an Accounting Software

When it comes to choosing accounting software, there are a few key things to look for.

  • Ease of use: You don't want to get bogged down in a complicated system with a steep learning curve. The software should be intuitive and user-friendly right out of the gate.
  • Reporting and analytics capabilities: These will allow you to really dig into the numbers and get valuable insights into your business's financial performance. You'll be able to easily generate things like profit and loss statements, balance sheets, and cash flow reports.
  • Integration: Ideally, the accounting software should seamlessly sync with any other systems or apps you use, whether it's payroll, inventory management, or eCommerce platforms. This eliminates duplicate data entry and manual transferring between platforms.
  • Scalability: As your business grows, you'll want accounting software that can scale up with you. You'll need solutions offering different service tiers and added functionality as your needs evolve.
  • Mobile accessibility: In our on-the-go world, it's super convenient to be able to view financial data, send invoices, and reconcile accounts from anywhere on your smartphone or tablet.
  • Support and training resources: To maximize the software, you'll want a knowledgeable team you can lean on, along with tutorials, guides, and forums.

» Still undecided? Discover why accounting software is worth it.

How We Determined the Top Quicken Alternatives

Our team tested and evaluated over 15 different accounting software options using the following criteria:

  • Ease of use: We sought interfaces that make navigation intuitive and data entry smooth. Software requiring extensive manual reading or lengthy tutorials didn't make the cut.
  • Reporting capabilities: We prioritized options that produce clean, comprehensive reports for income statements, cash flow, and tax liabilities. We avoided solutions with limited or confusing reporting.
  • Integration: The top alternatives seamlessly connect with other essential business tools. We avoided standalone options that couldn't sync with your existing systems.
  • Mobility: Access to key financial data, bill payments, and account reconciliation via mobile apps or browsers was a significant factor in our evaluation.
  • Pricing: We focused on solutions that offer great value, with transparent fee structures and flexible pricing tiers to accommodate your business growth.

Quicken Alternatives: The Accounting Software for Your Business Needs

With evolving economies, business demands and our financial needs grow. Overall, Oracle NetSuite is the most comprehensive Quicken alternative. FreshBooks caters excellently to freelancers and solopreneurs, while Zoho Books shines for small to medium businesses.

1-800Accountant provides expert tax/finance advice, and Patriot Software seamlessly integrates HR and accounting. Ultimately, the right accounting software depends on whether it suits your unique requirements. This knowledge will help you make the best choice.

FAQs

What's the best alternative to Quicken?

Oracle NetSuite stands out as a robust option for businesses seeking an alternative to Quicken. It offers a full suite of enterprise resource planning (ERP) features, including advanced financial management, inventory control, and business intelligence capabilities.

Is Quicken being phased out?

No, Quicken is not being phased out. Quicken continues to be actively developed and supported by its parent company, with regular updates and new versions released. While there have been changes in ownership and product offerings over the years, Quicken remains a popular personal finance management tool.

Which Quicken alternative is best for freelancers?

FreshBooks is the top choice for freelancers and solopreneurs. It offers intuitive invoicing, time tracking, and expense management features tailored for self-employed professionals. FreshBooks also integrates with many popular business tools.

Is there a Quicken alternative that combines accounting and HR?

Patriot Software is an excellent option for integrated HR and accounting. It offers payroll, time tracking, and basic accounting features in one platform. This integration can streamline operations for small businesses managing both finance and human resources.

What's a good Quicken alternative for growing SMBs?

Zoho Books is well-suited for small—to medium-sized businesses experiencing growth. It offers scalable features, multiple-user access, and integrations with other Zoho products, and it can accommodate increasing complexity as your business expands.

Bottom line: For small businesses just starting out, Simple Start now functions more like a smart assistant than a static bookkeeping tool.

Essentials: AI-Powered CRM & Payments Automation for Growing Teams

Plus: Reconciliation, Anomaly Detection, and Full CRM Expansion

This version goes deeper than the Essentials tier, handling not just categorization but also AI-powered reconciliation and anomaly detection. It flags anything suspicious in your books and suggests corrective actions.

  • Reconciliation (Beta) & Anomaly Detection:

  • Insights: P&L and Balance Sheet Visualizations:

Advanced: Financial Agents, KPI Dashboards & Pro-Level Features

QuickBooks has taken a significant step toward becoming more than just accounting software. By embedding smart agents, integrated CRM features, and powerful automation across every tier, it now functions more like a full-scale business operating system.

Top 10 Benefits of Outsourcing Healthcare Accounting Services

  • Scalability: Your chosen accounting software should be able to scale with your business, meeting your financial needs as you continue to grow.   • Remote access: Most modern accounting software providers offer online or remote access. This allows your external accountant to access, track, and update your financial records anytime, anywhere. How to Mitigate Potential Drawbacks of Outsourcing Accounting Software

Outsourcing accounting services can be an important strategic decision for healthcare organizations.
